meta.title: TechFuelHQ GPU Undervolt Settings and Attributed Results
meta.description: Eight GPU undervolt entries: five community-consensus setting references with null outcomes and three attributed reports. These are not eight verified experiments or a sample of typical savings.
meta.contribute: A GitHub account is required to submit a pull request to https://github.com/iBlessi/gpu-undervolt-db. Email hello@techfuelhq.com as an alternative. Include settings, a source and measured outcomes; leave unmeasured values null.

fields.gpu: canonical card model, e.g. 'RTX 5080' or 'RX 9070 XT'
fields.board: Board variant named by the reference or report, or '' if unspecified
fields.tbp_watts: stock total board power in watts
fields.method: MSI Afterburner V/F curve (NVIDIA) or AMD Adrenalin voltage offset/max-voltage (AMD)
fields.setting: Settings described by the reference or attributed report; not a stability guarantee
fields.voltage_mv: NVIDIA curve target voltage, or AMD RDNA3 absolute max voltage, in mV (nullable)
fields.offset_mv: AMD negative voltage offset in mV, RDNA4 (nullable)
fields.power_limit_pct: power limit applied; percent of stock for NVIDIA (e.g. 90) or delta for AMD (e.g. -10 or +15); null if untouched
fields.power_saved_w: Reported stock-minus-tuned board power in watts for the stated workload; null means unavailable, zero means no reported change
fields.temp_drop_c: Reported hotspot/junction temperature drop in C; null means unavailable, zero means no reported change
fields.fps_delta_pct: Reported performance change versus stock in percent: positive gain, zero parity, negative loss; may summarize a benchmark rather than game FPS (see test_method); null means unavailable
fields.stability_hours: Reported stable test duration in hours; null means no duration established
fields.test_method: Source attribution, workload and measurement limits; consensus rows describe reference instructions, not completed tests
fields.source_type: Provenance category: community-consensus is a setting reference; community-verified and review-measured here are attributed external reports, not TechFuelHQ validation; editorial-firstparty and community-submitted are reserved for such submissions
fields.source_url: Primary reference or report for the row
fields.submitter: Who compiled or submitted the row, with original attribution
fields.date: YYYY-MM-DD the row was added or corrected; not the experiment date
fields.flagged: true if the outlier-flag script flagged this row (do not set by hand)
fields.flag_reason: why it was flagged (set by the script)

results.test_method: Setting reference from the linked TechFuelHQ guide. No configuration-specific before/after measurement or stability duration is established; outcomes are null.
results.submitter: TechFuelHQ (published community range, not a logged first-party run)

results.setting: -100 mV offset (power limit left at stock)
results.test_method: XDA attributes roughly +10% performance to its Sapphire NITRO+ tuning report at -100 mV. This is an author-reported result, not a standardized cross-card benchmark; power, temperature deltas and stability duration are not established in this row.
results.submitter: TechFuelHQ (compiled from the XDA author report; secondary r/radeon discussion)

results.test_method: Community setting reference from the linked discussion and power-limit coverage. Those sources do not establish outcomes for this exact voltage, clock and memory combination.
Setting reference from the linked guides. Their game and ray-tracing checks are instructions; no measured outcomes or completed stability duration are established for this row.

results.setting: 900 mV @ 2800 MHz (flatten curve above the point)
results.test_method: Setting reference from the linked discussion and guide. Testing demanding games is recommended there; no configuration-specific results or test duration are established here.

results.setting: 935 mV @ 2955 MHz (via +450 MHz core offset), +1500 memory
results.test_method: Esports Tales reports 935 mV / 2955 MHz with +1500 memory on its ASUS Prime OC. The 50 W saving is 300 W stock minus 250 W tuned in Steel Nomad, not a cross-game constant. The author summarizes performance at approximately +4% and power savings at 50-70 W across workloads; no fixed stability duration is supplied.
results.submitter: TechFuelHQ (community-sourced: Esports Tales hands-on + MSI guide)

results.setting: 1100 mV max voltage (~-50 mV vs ~1150 mV stock), power limit +15%
results.test_method: Setting reference from the linked guide and user discussion. Voltage steps and stress checks are reference instructions, not a completed test of this configuration.

Notebookcheck reports Alva Jonathan testing Cyberpunk 2077 at 54 FPS stock versus 50 FPS tuned with -100 mV and -30% power limit. The retained -7% is rounded from (50/54 - 1) x 100, rather than the article prose calling it about 10%. No stability duration or matched power measurement is recorded here.
results.submitter: TechFuelHQ (Alva Jonathan result as reported by Notebookcheck; not a Notebookcheck bench)
